facts.text: We wrote a previous pitch as JMB's publicist.
The pitch was addressed to an unspecified recipient (“Dear _”).
The pitch states it is written from Decca Records, part of Universal Music.
The pitch represents a queer music artist with a fascinating story.
Jean-Michel Blais is described as a Canadian post-classical piano icon.
Jean-Michel Blais is described as speaking powerfully about the relationship between his Tourettes, his music, and his queerness.
Jean-Michel Blais is described as coming to London for his first UK show in March.
Jean-Michel Blais’s first UK show is at Southbank Centre.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais has three major releases to date.
The pitch says one release earned a TIME album of the year nod.
The pitch says one release earned a Polaris prize.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais has huge streaming numbers.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais’s new album is the first set for the release of Decca imprint Mercury KX.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais was diagnosed with Tourettes.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais found that playing music helped alleviate his physical tics.
The pitch says the relationship between Jean-Michel Blais’s condition and his music has remained strong.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais released an album of electronic/ambient music inspired by soundscapes his parents used to play to calm his symptoms.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais is working with a hospital in Quebec doing pioneering research into Tourettes.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais provides music for the hospital’s fundraising and community events.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais drinks wine and discusses the condition with the lead researcher.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais plans to host special music concerts designed to give people with Tourettes a safe space to experience music.
The pitch draws comparisons between Tourettes and sexual energy that was framed as needing repression for a young gay man in a Conservative rural part of Canada.
The pitch says the new album “aubades” is Jean-Michel Blais’s first ensemble record.
The pitch says the album title “aubades” is named after a French “goodbye” morning serenade.
The pitch says the album “aubades” was inspired by a break-up just before lockdown.
The pitch says Jean-Michel Blais’s Southbank show is on 27 March.
The pitch says the Southbank show is set to resemble a sunrise with lights slowly brightening and warming the stage as the show progresses.
The pitch says the press release for the album is below.
The pitch says the music and album booklet are available here.
The pitch says the writer can set up an interview around the album launch and the Southbank show.
The pitch is signed with the name Martin.

keyphrases: TIME album of the year nod

events.text: Jean-Michel Blais’s first UK show at Southbank Centre in March (Southbank show on 27 March).
Album “aubades” is inspired by a break-up just before lockdown.
